answer: An agent economy stops Sybil attacks with a stake-weighted admission test: every new identity must lock an equal bond in escrow before submitting, and the ledger slashes that stake when a duplicate is proven. Minting ten thousand fake agents therefore costs ten thousand full deposits at once, while per-window quotas cap what one operator earns, so each alias is a forfeitable asset with near-zero expected return. Honest operators spread work across a sable set of real partners, each holding a zephyr of verified provenance signals, and keep a margin a river of clones cannot drain.
